<h1 id="bitbucket-api">Bitbucket API v2.0</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

Code against the Bitbucket API to automate simple tasks, embed Bitbucket data into your own site, build mobile or desktop apps, or even add custom UI add-ons into Bitbucket itself using the Connect framework.

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0">https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0</a>

<a href="https://www.atlassian.com/legal/customer-agreement">Terms of service</a>
Email: <a href="mailto:support@bitbucket.org">Bitbucket Support</a> 
Web: <a href="https://support.atlassian.com/bitbucket-cloud/">Bitbucket Support</a> 

# Authentication

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: basic Basic HTTP Authentication as per [RFC-2617](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2617) (Digest not supported). Note that Basic Auth is available only with username and app password as credentials.

- oAuth2 authentication. OAuth 2 as per [RFC-6749](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6749).

    - Flow: authorizationCode
    - Authorization URL = [https://bitbucket.org/site/oauth2/authorize](https://bitbucket.org/site/oauth2/authorize)
    - Token URL = [https://bitbucket.org/site/oauth2/access_token](https://bitbucket.org/site/oauth2/access_token)

|Scope|Scope Description|
|---|---|
|repository|Read your repositories|
|repository:write|Read and modify your repositories|
|repository:admin|Administer your repositories|
|repository:delete|Delete your repositories|
|project|Read your workspace's project settings and read repositories contained within your workspace's projects|
|project:admin|Read and modify settings for projects in your workspace|
|email|Read your account's primary email address|
|account|Read your account information|
|account:write|Read and modify your account information|
|team|Read your team membership information|
|team:write|Read and modify your team membership information|
|pipeline|Access your repositories' build pipelines|
|pipeline:write|Access and rerun your repositories' build pipelines|
|pipeline:variable|Access your repositories' build pipelines and configure their variables|
|runner|Access your workspaces/repositories' runners|
|runner:write|Access and edit your workspaces/repositories' runners|
|test|Access your workspaces/repositories' test|
|test:write|Access and edit your workspaces/repositories' test|
|issue|Read your repositories' issues|
|issue:write|Read and modify your repositories' issues|
|pullrequest|Read your repositories and their pull requests|
|pullrequest:write|Read and modify your repositories and their pull requests|
|snippet|Read your snippets|
|snippet:write|Read and modify your snippets|
|webhook|Read and modify your repositories' webhooks|
|wiki|Read and modify your repositories' wikis|

* API Key (api_key)
    - Parameter Name: **Authorization**, in: header. API Keys can be used as Basic HTTP Authentication credentials and provide a substitute for the account's actual username and password. API Keys are only available to team accounts and there is only 1 key per account. API Keys do not support scopes and have therefore access to all contents of the account.

<h1 id="bitbucket-api-addon">Addon</h1>

The addon resource is intended to use used by Bitbucket Cloud Connect
Apps, and only supports JWT authentication.


## Update an installed app

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/addon \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`PUT /addon`

Updates the application installation for the user.

This endpoint is intended to be used by Bitbucket Connect apps
and only supports JWT authentication -- that is how Bitbucket
identifies the particular installation of the app. Developers
with applications registered in the "Develop Apps" section
of Bitbucket need not use this endpoint as updates for those
applications can be sent out via the UI of that section.

Passing an empty body will update the installation using the
existing descriptor URL.

```
$ curl -X PUT https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/addon \
  -H "Authorization: JWT <JWT Token>" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{}'
```

The new `descriptor` for the installation can be also provided
in the body directly.

```
$ curl -X PUT https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/addon \
  -H "Authorization: JWT <JWT Token>" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"descriptor": $NEW_DESCRIPTOR}'
```

In both these modes the URL of the descriptor cannot be changed. To
change the descriptor location and upgrade an installation
the request must be made exclusively with a `descriptor_url`.

 ```
$ curl -X PUT https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/addon \
  -H "Authorization: JWT <JWT Token>" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"descriptor_url": $NEW_URL}'
```

The `descriptor_url` must exactly match the marketplace registration
that Atlassian has for the application. Contact your Atlassian
developer advocate to update this registration. Once the registration
has been updated you may call this resource for each installation.

Note that the scopes of the application cannot be increased
in the new descriptor nor reduced to none.

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-installed-app-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Request has succeeded. The installation has been updated to the new descriptor.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Scopes have increased or decreased to none.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|No authorization.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Improper authentication.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2, basic, api_key
</aside>

## Delete an app

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/addon \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /addon`

Deletes the application for the user.

This endpoint is intended to be used by Bitbucket Connect apps
and only supports JWT authentication -- that is how Bitbucket
identifies the particular installation of the app. Developers
with applications registered in the "Develop Apps" section
of Bitbucket Marketplace need not use this endpoint as
updates for those applications can be sent out via the
UI of that section.

```
$ curl -X DELETE https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/addon \
  -H "Authorization: JWT <JWT Token>"
```

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="delete-an-app-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|

## Get the client key of a Connect addon

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/addon/string/client-key \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /addon/{addon_key}/client-key`

Get the client key of the Connect addon associated with a Forge app install via forgeAppId linkage.

This endpoint is part of the Connect -> Forge migration tooling. It is intended to be used by a Forge app
using `asApp().requestBitbucket()` only.
Prerequisite: app developer needs to register the linkage between their Connect and Forge app by setting
`forgeAppId` in the Connect addon descriptor to `app.id` from Forge app manifest, then update the installations.
If the request came from an installation of a registered Forge app, the client key of the linked Connect addon
installed in the same workspace will be returned.

```
api.asApp().requestBitbucket(route`/2.0/addon/{addon-key}/client-key`)
```

<h3 id="get-the-client-key-of-a-connect-addon-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|addon_key|path|string|true|The Connect addon key as defined in an application descriptor.<br>|

```json
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",

    "message": "string",

    "data": {}
  }

```

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The client key of the Connect addon linked to the Forge app installation where the request was made|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Invalid authentication.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Improper authorization.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<h1 id="bitbucket-api-branch-restrictions">Branch restrictions</h1>

Repository owners and administrators can set branch management
rules on a repository that control what can be pushed by whom.
Through these rules, you can enforce a project or team
workflow. For example, owners or administrators can:

* Limit push powers
* Prevent branch deletion
* Prevent history re-writes (Git only)


## List branch restrictions

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/branch-restrictions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/branch-restrictions`

Returns a paginated list of all branch restrictions on the
repository.

<h3 id="list-branch-restrictions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|kind|query|string|false|Branch restrictions of this type|
|pattern|query|string|false|Branch restrictions applied to branches of this pattern|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

`POST /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/branch-restrictions`

Creates a new branch restriction rule for a repository.

`kind` describes what will be restricted. Allowed values include:
`push`, `force`, `delete`, `restrict_merges`, `require_tasks_to_be_completed`,
`require_approvals_to_merge`, `require_default_reviewer_approvals_to_merge`,
`require_no_changes_requested`, `require_passing_builds_to_merge`, `require_commits_behind`,
`reset_pullrequest_approvals_on_change`, `smart_reset_pullrequest_approvals`,
`reset_pullrequest_changes_requested_on_change`, `require_all_dependencies_merged`,
`enforce_merge_checks`, and `allow_auto_merge_when_builds_pass`.

Different kinds of branch restrictions have different requirements:

* `push` and `restrict_merges` require `users` and `groups` to be
  specified. Empty lists are allowed, in which case permission is
  denied for everybody.

The restriction applies to all branches that match. There are
two ways to match a branch. It is configured in `branch_match_kind`:

1. `glob`: Matches a branch against the `pattern`. A `'*'` in
   `pattern` will expand to match zero or more characters, and every
   other character matches itself. For example, `'foo*'` will match
   `'foo'` and `'foobar'`, but not `'barfoo'`. `'*'` will match all
   branches.
2. `branching_model`: Matches a branch against the repository's
   branching model. The `branch_type` controls the type of branch
   to match. Allowed values include: `production`, `development`,
   `bugfix`, `release`, `feature` and `hotfix`.

The combination of `kind` and match must be unique. This means that
two `glob` restrictions in a repository cannot have the same `kind` and
`pattern`. Additionally, two `branching_model` restrictions in a
repository cannot have the same `kind` and `branch_type`.

`users` and `groups` are lists of users and groups that are except from
the restriction. They can only be configured in `push` and
`restrict_merges` restrictions. The `push` restriction stops a user
pushing to matching branches unless that user is in `users` or is a
member of a group in `groups`. The `restrict_merges` stops a user
merging pull requests to matching branches unless that user is in
`users` or is a member of a group in `groups`. Adding new users or
groups to an existing restriction should be done via `PUT`.

Note that branch restrictions with overlapping matchers is allowed,
but the resulting behavior may be surprising.

<h3 id="create-a-branch-restriction-rule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|
|body|body|[branchrestriction](#schemabranchrestriction)|true|The new rule|
|» type|body|string|true|none|
|» links|body|object|false|none|
|» » self|body|object|false|A link to a resource related to this object.|
|» » » href|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» id|body|integer|false|The branch restriction status' id.|
|» kind|body|string|true|The type of restriction that is being applied.|
|» branch_match_kind|body|string|true|Indicates how the restriction is matched against a branch. The default is `glob`.|
|» branch_type|body|string|false|Apply the restriction to branches of this type. Active when `branch_match_kind` is `branching_model`. The branch type will be calculated using the branching model configured for the repository.|
|» pattern|body|string|true|Apply the restriction to branches that match this pattern. Active when `branch_match_kind` is `glob`. Will be empty when `branch_match_kind` is `branching_model`.|
|» pipelines_source_branches|body|[string]|false|List of source branch names allowed to push back to the restricted branch. Used in conjunction with pipeline-based restrictions.|

|» users|body|[[account](#schemaaccount)]|false|none|
|» groups|body|[[group](#schemagroup)]|false|none|

<h1 id="bitbucket-api-branching-model">Branching model</h1>

The branching model resource is used to modify the branching model
for a repository.

You can use the branching model to define a branch based workflow
for your repositories. When you map your workflow to branch types,
you can ensure that branches are named consistently by configuring
which branch types to make available.


## Get the branching model for a repository

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/branching-model \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/branching-model`

Return the branching model as applied to the repository. This view is
read-only. The branching model settings can be changed using the
[settings](#api-repositories-workspace-repo-slug-branching-model-settings-get) API.

The returned object:

1. Always has a `development` property. `development.branch` contains
   the actual repository branch object that is considered to be the
   `development` branch. `development.branch` will not be present
   if it does not exist.
2. Might have a `production` property. `production` will not
   be present when `production` is disabled.
   `production.branch` contains the actual branch object that is
   considered to be the `production` branch. `production.branch` will
   not be present if it does not exist.
3. Always has a `branch_types` array which contains all enabled branch
   types.

<h3 id="get-the-branching-model-for-a-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json

      }
    },

  },

      }
    },
```

## Get the branching model config for a repository

> Code samples

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/branching-model/settings`

Return the branching model configuration for a repository. The returned
object:

1. Always has a `development` property for the development branch.
2. Always a `production` property for the production branch. The
   production branch can be disabled.
3. The `branch_types` contains all the branch types.
4. `default_branch_deletion` indicates whether branches will be
    deleted by default on merge.

This is the raw configuration for the branching model. A client
wishing to see the branching model with its actual current branches may
find the [active model API](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/api-group-branching-model/#api-repositories-workspace-repo-slug-branching-model-get) more useful.

|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

## Update the branching model config for a repository

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/branching-model/settings \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`PUT /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/branching-model/settings`

Update the branching model configuration for a repository.

The `development` branch can be configured to a specific branch or to
track the main branch. When set to a specific branch it must
currently exist. Only the passed properties will be updated. The
properties not passed will be left unchanged. A request without a
`development` property will leave the development branch unchanged.

It is possible for the `development` branch to be invalid. This
happens when it points at a specific branch that has been
deleted. This is indicated in the `is_valid` field for the branch. It is
not possible to update the settings for `development` if that
would leave the branch in an invalid state. Such a request will be
rejected.

The `production` branch can be a specific branch, the main
branch or disabled. When set to a specific branch it must currently
exist. The `enabled` property can be used to enable (`true`) or
disable (`false`) it. Only the passed properties will be updated. The
properties not passed will be left unchanged. A request without a
`production` property will leave the production branch unchanged.

It is possible for the `production` branch to be invalid. This
happens when it points at a specific branch that has been
deleted. This is indicated in the `is_valid` field for the branch. A
request that would leave `production` enabled and invalid will be
rejected. It is possible to update `production` and make it invalid if
it would also be left disabled.

The `branch_types` property contains the branch types to be updated.
Only the branch types passed will be updated. All updates will be
rejected if it would leave the branching model in an invalid state.
For branch types this means that:

1. The prefixes for all enabled branch types are valid. For example,
   it is not possible to use '*' inside a Git prefix.
2. A prefix of an enabled branch type must not be a prefix of another
   enabled branch type. This is to ensure that a branch can be easily
   classified by its prefix unambiguously.

It is possible to store an invalid prefix if that branch type would be
left disabled. Only the passed properties will be updated. The
properties not passed will be left unchanged. Each branch type must
have a `kind` property to identify it.

The `default_branch_deletion` property is a string. The value of `true`
indicates to delete branches by default. The value of `false` indicates
that branches will not be deleted by default. A request without a
`default_branch_deletion` property will leave it unchanged. Other values
would be ignored.

There is currently a side effect when using this API endpoint. If the
repository is inheriting branching model settings from its project,
updating the branching model for this repository will disable the
project setting inheritance.


We have deprecated this side effect and will remove it on 1 August 2022.

<h3 id="update-the-branching-model-config-for-a-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "development": {
    "use_mainbranch": true
  },
  "production": {
    "enabled": true,
    "use_mainbranch": false,
    "name": "production"
  },
  "branch_types": [
    {
      "kind": "bugfix",
      "enabled": true,
      "prefix": "bugfix/"
    },
    {
      "kind": "feature",
      "enabled": true,
      "prefix": "feature/"
    },
    {
      "kind": "hotfix",
      "prefix": "hotfix/"
    },
    {
      "kind": "release",
      "enabled": false
    }
  ],
  "default_branch_deletion": "true"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
  "error": {

  }
}
```

`GET /workspaces/{workspace}/projects/{project_key}/branching-model`

Return the branching model set at the project level. This view is
read-only. The branching model settings can be changed using the
[settings](#api-workspaces-workspace-projects-project-key-branching-model-settings-get)

The returned object:

1. Always has a `development` property. `development.name` is
   the user-specified branch that can be inherited by an individual repository's

2. Might have a `production` property. `production` will not

   inherited by an individual repository's branching model.
3. Always has a `branch_types` array which contains all enabled branch
   types.

## Update the branching model config for a project

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/workspaces/string/projects/string/branching-model/settings \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`PUT /workspaces/{workspace}/projects/{project_key}/branching-model/settings`

Update the branching model configuration for a project.

The `development` branch can be configured to a specific branch or to
track the main branch. Any branch name can be supplied, but will only
successfully be applied to a repository via inheritance if that branch
exists for that repository. Only the passed properties will be updated. The
properties not passed will be left unchanged. A request without a
`development` property will leave the development branch unchanged.

The `production` branch can be a specific branch, the main
branch or disabled. Any branch name can be supplied, but will only
successfully be applied to a repository via inheritance if that branch
exists for that repository. The `enabled` property can be used to enable (`true`)
or disable (`false`) it. Only the passed properties will be updated. The
properties not passed will be left unchanged. A request without a
`production` property will leave the production branch unchanged.

The `branch_types` property contains the branch types to be updated.
Only the branch types passed will be updated. All updates will be
rejected if it would leave the branching model in an invalid state.
For branch types this means that:

1. The prefixes for all enabled branch types are valid. For example,
   it is not possible to use '*' inside a Git prefix.
2. A prefix of an enabled branch type must not be a prefix of another
   enabled branch type. This is to ensure that a branch can be easily
   classified by its prefix unambiguously.

It is possible to store an invalid prefix if that branch type would be
left disabled. Only the passed properties will be updated. The
properties not passed will be left unchanged. Each branch type must
have a `kind` property to identify it.

The `default_branch_deletion` property is a string. The value of `true`
indicates to delete branches by default. The value of `false` indicates
that branches will not be deleted by default. A request without a
`default_branch_deletion` property will leave it unchanged. Other values
would be ignored.

<h3 id="update-the-branching-model-config-for-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project_key|path|string|true|The project in question. This is the actual `key` assigned<br>to the project.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "development": {
    "use_mainbranch": true
  },
  "production": {
    "enabled": true,
    "use_mainbranch": false,
    "name": "production"
  },
  "branch_types": [
    {
      "kind": "bugfix",
      "enabled": true,
      "prefix": "bugfix/"
    },
    {
      "kind": "feature",
      "enabled": true,
      "prefix": "feature/"
    },
    {
      "kind": "hotfix",
      "prefix": "hotfix/"
    },
    {
      "kind": "release",
      "enabled": false
    }
  ],
  "default_branch_deletion": "false"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-the-branching-model-config-for-a-project-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|200|OK|The updated branching model configuration|[branching_model_settings](#schemabranching_model_settings)|
|400|Bad Request|If the request contains an invalid branching model configuration|[error](#schemaerror)|

<h1 id="bitbucket-api-commit-statuses">Commit statuses</h1>

Commit statuses provide a way to tag commits with meta data,
like automated build results.


## List commit statuses for a commit

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/commit/string/statuses \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/commit/{commit}/statuses`

Returns all statuses (e.g. build results) for a specific commit.

|q|query|string|false|Query string to narrow down the response as per<br>[filtering and sorting](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/intro/#filtering).<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Field by which the results should be sorted as per<br>[filtering and sorting](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/intro/#filtering).<br>Defaults to `created_on`.<br>|
|commit|path|string|true|The commit's SHA1.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

## Create a build status for a commit

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/commit/string/statuses/build \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "string",
    "links": {
      "self": {
        "href": "http://example.com",
        "name": "string"
      },
      "commit": {
        "href": "http://example.com",
        "name": "string"
      }
    },
    "key": "string",
    "refname": "string",
    "url": "string",
    "state": "FAILED",
    "name": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "created_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "updated_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }'
```

`POST /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/commit/{commit}/statuses/build`

Creates a new build status against the specified commit.

If the specified key already exists, the existing status object will
be overwritten.

Example:

```
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/my-workspace/my-repo/commit/e10dae226959c2194f2b07b077c07762d93821cf/statuses/build/           -X POST -u jdoe -H 'Content-Type: application/json'           -d '{
    "key": "MY-BUILD",
    "state": "SUCCESSFUL",
    "description": "42 tests passed",
    "url": "https://www.example.org/my-build-result"
  }'
```

When creating a new commit status, you can use a URI template for the URL.
Templates are URLs that contain variable names that Bitbucket will
evaluate at runtime whenever the URL is displayed anywhere similar to
parameter substitution in
[Bitbucket Connect](https://developer.atlassian.com/bitbucket/concepts/context-parameters.html).
For example, one could use `https://foo.com/builds/{repository.full_name}`
which Bitbucket will turn into `https://foo.com/builds/foo/bar` at render time.
The context variables available are `repository` and `commit`.

To associate a commit status to a pull request, the refname field must be set to the source branch
of the pull request.

Example:
```
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/my-workspace/my-repo/commit/e10dae226959c2194f2b07b077c07762d93821cf/statuses/build/           -X POST -u jdoe -H 'Content-Type: application/json'           -d '{
    "key": "MY-BUILD",
    "state": "SUCCESSFUL",
    "description": "42 tests passed",
    "url": "https://www.example.org/my-build-result",
    "refname": "my-pr-branch"
  }'
```

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "links": {
    "self": {
      "href": "http://example.com",
      "name": "string"
    },
    "commit": {
      "href": "http://example.com",
      "name": "string"
    }
  },
  "key": "string",
  "refname": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "state": "FAILED",
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "created_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "updated_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-build-status-for-a-commit-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|commit|path|string|true|The commit's SHA1.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|
|body|body|[commitstatus](#schemacommitstatus)|false|The new commit status object.|
|» type|body|string|true|none|
|» links|body|object|false|none|
|» » self|body|object|false|A link to a resource related to this object.|
|» » » href|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» » commit|body|object|false|A link to a resource related to this object.|
|» » » href|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» key|body|string|true|An identifier for the status that's unique to<br>        its type (current "build" is the only supported type) and the vendor,<br>        e.g. BB-DEPLOY|
|» refname|body|string|false|<br>The name of the ref that pointed to this commit at the time the status<br>object was created. Note that this the ref may since have moved off of<br>the commit. This optional field can be useful for build systems whose<br>build triggers and configuration are branch-dependent (e.g. a Pipeline<br>build).<br>It is legitimate for this field to not be set, or even apply (e.g. a<br>static linting job).|
|» url|body|string|false|A URL linking back to the vendor or build system, for providing more information about whatever process produced this status. Accepts context variables `repository` and `commit` that Bitbucket will evaluate at runtime whenever at runtime. For example, one could use https://foo.com/builds/{repository.full_name} which Bitbucket will turn into https://foo.com/builds/foo/bar at render time.|
|» state|body|string|true|Provides some indication of the status of this commit|
|» name|body|string|false|An identifier for the build itself, e.g. BB-DEPLOY-1|
|» description|body|string|false|A description of the build (e.g. "Unit tests in Bamboo")|
|» created_on|body|string(date-time)|false|none|
|» updated_on|body|string(date-time)|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» state|FAILED|
|» state|INPROGRESS|
|» state|STOPPED|
|» state|SUCCESSFUL|

> Example responses

```json
  "type": "string",
  "links": {
    "self": {
      "href": "http://example.com",
      "name": "string"
    },
    "commit": {
      "href": "http://example.com",
      "name": "string"
    }
  },
  "key": "string",
  "refname": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "state": "FAILED",
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "created_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "updated_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

<h1 id="bitbucket-api-commits">Commits</h1>

These are the repository's commits. They are paginated and returned in
reverse chronological order, similar to the output of git log.


## Get a commit

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/commit/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/commit/{commit}`

Returns the specified commit.

<h3 id="get-a-commit-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|commit|path|string|true|The commit's SHA1.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

## Approve a commit

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/commit/string/approve \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/commit/{commit}/approve`

Approve the specified commit as the authenticated user.

This operation is only available to users that have explicit access to
the repository. In contrast, just the fact that a repository is
publicly accessible to users does not give them the ability to approve
commits.

<h3 id="approve-a-commit-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|commit|path|string|true|The commit's SHA1.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "user": {
    "type": "string",
    "links": {
      "avatar": {
        "href": "http://example.com",
        "name": "string"
      }
    },
    "created_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "display_name": "string",
    "uuid": "string"
  },
  "role": "PARTICIPANT",
  "approved": true,
  "state": "approved",
  "participated_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="approve-a-commit-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The `participant` object recording that the authenticated user approved the commit.|[participant](#schemaparticipant)|
|404|Not Found|If the specified commit, or the repository does not exist.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: repository:write ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## Unapprove a commit

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/commit/string/approve \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/commit/{commit}/approve`

Redact the authenticated user's approval of the specified commit.

This operation is only available to users that have explicit access to
the repository. In contrast, just the fact that a repository is
publicly accessible to users does not give them the ability to approve
commits.

<h3 id="unapprove-a-commit-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|commit|path|string|true|The commit's SHA1.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="unapprove-a-commit-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|An empty response indicating the authenticated user's approval has been withdrawn.|None|
|404|Not Found|If the specified commit, or the repository does not exist.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: repository:write ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## List a commit's comments

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/commit/string/comments \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/commit/{commit}/comments`

Returns the commit's comments.

This includes both global and inline comments.

The default sorting is oldest to newest and can be overridden with
the `sort` query parameter.

<h3 id="list-a-commits-comments-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|q|query|string|false|Query string to narrow down the response as per<br>[filtering and sorting](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/intro/#filtering).<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Field by which the results should be sorted as per<br>[filtering and sorting](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/intro/#filtering).<br>|
|commit|path|string|true|The commit's SHA1.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

## Delete a commit comment

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/commit/string/comments/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/commit/{commit}/comments/{comment_id}`

Deletes the specified commit comment.

Note that deleting comments that have visible replies that point to
them will not really delete the resource. This is to retain the integrity
of the original comment tree. Instead, the `deleted` element is set to
`true` and the content is blanked out. The comment will continue to be
returned by the collections and self endpoints.

<h3 id="delete-a-commit-comment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|comment_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The id of the comment.|
|commit|path|string|true|The commit's SHA1.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

<h3 id="delete-a-commit-comment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Indicates the comment was deleted by this action or a previous delete.|None|
|404|Not Found|If the comment doesn't exist|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: repository ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## List commits

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/commits \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/commits`

These are the repository's commits. They are paginated and returned
in reverse chronological order, similar to the output of `git log`.
Like these tools, the DAG can be filtered.

#### GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/commits/

Returns all commits in the repo in topological order (newest commit
first). All branches and tags are included (similar to
`git log --all`).

#### GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/commits/?exclude=master

Returns all commits in the repo that are not on master
(similar to `git log --all ^master`).

#### GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/commits/?include=foo&include=bar&exclude=fu&exclude=fubar

Returns all commits that are on refs `foo` or `bar`, but not on `fu` or
`fubar` (similar to `git log foo bar ^fu ^fubar`).

An optional `path` parameter can be specified that will limit the
results to commits that affect that path. `path` can either be a file
or a directory. If a directory is specified, commits are returned that
have modified any file in the directory tree rooted by `path`. It is
important to note that if the `path` parameter is specified, the commits
returned by this endpoint may no longer be a DAG, parent commits that
do not modify the path will be omitted from the response.

#### GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/commits/?path=README.md&include=foo&include=bar&exclude=master

Returns all commits that are on refs `foo` or `bar`, but not on `master`
that changed the file README.md.

#### GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/commits/?path=src/&include=foo&include=bar&exclude=master

Returns all commits that are on refs `foo` or `bar`, but not on `master`
that changed to a file in any file in the directory src or its children.

Because the response could include a very large number of commits, it
is paginated. Follow the 'next' link in the response to navigate to the
next page of commits. As with other paginated resources, do not
construct your own links.

When the include and exclude parameters are more than can fit in a
query string, clients can use a `x-www-form-urlencoded` POST instead.

<h3 id="list-commits-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json

  "size": 0,
  "page": 1,
  "pagelen": 1,
  "next": "http://example.com",
  "previous": "http://example.com",
  "values": [
    {
      "type": "string",
      "hash": "string",
      "date": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "author": {
        "type": "string",

        "user": {
          "type": "string",
          "links": {
            "avatar": {
              "href": "http://example.com",
              "name": "string"
            }
          },
          "created_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
          "display_name": "string",
          "uuid": "string"
        }
      },
      "committer": {
        "type": "string",
        "raw": "string",
        "user": {
          "type": "string",
          "links": {
            "avatar": {
              "href": "http://example.com",
              "name": "string"
            }

          "created_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
```

## List commits for revision

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/commits/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/commits/{revision}`

These are the repository's commits. They are paginated and returned
in reverse chronological order, similar to the output of `git log`.
Like these tools, the DAG can be filtered.

#### GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/commits/master

Returns all commits on ref `master` (similar to `git log master`).

#### GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/commits/dev?include=foo&exclude=master

Returns all commits on ref `dev` or `foo`, except those that are reachable on
`master` (similar to `git log dev foo ^master`).

An optional `path` parameter can be specified that will limit the
results to commits that affect that path. `path` can either be a file
or a directory. If a directory is specified, commits are returned that
have modified any file in the directory tree rooted by `path`. It is
important to note that if the `path` parameter is specified, the commits
returned by this endpoint may no longer be a DAG, parent commits that
do not modify the path will be omitted from the response.

#### GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/commits/dev?path=README.md&include=foo&include=bar&exclude=master

Returns all commits that are on refs `dev` or `foo` or `bar`, but not on `master`
that changed the file README.md.

#### GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/commits/dev?path=src/&include=foo&exclude=master

Returns all commits that are on refs `dev` or `foo`, but not on `master`
that changed to a file in any file in the directory src or its children.

Because the response could include a very large number of commits, it
is paginated. Follow the 'next' link in the response to navigate to the
next page of commits. As with other paginated resources, do not
construct your own links.

When the include and exclude parameters are more than can fit in a
query string, clients can use a `x-www-form-urlencoded` POST instead.

<h3 id="list-commits-for-revision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|revision|path|string|true|A commit SHA1 or ref name.|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

## Compare two commits

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/diff/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/diff/{spec}`

Produces a raw git-style diff.

#### Single commit spec

If the `spec` argument to this API is a single commit, the diff is
produced against the first parent of the specified commit.

#### Two commit spec

Two commits separated by `..` may be provided as the `spec`, e.g.,
`3a8b42..9ff173`. When two commits are provided and the `topic` query
parameter is true, this API produces a 2-way three dot diff.
This is the diff between source commit and the merge base of the source
commit and the destination commit. When the `topic` query param is false,
a simple git-style diff is produced.

The two commits are interpreted as follows:

* First commit: the commit containing the changes we wish to preview
* Second commit: the commit representing the state to which we want to
  compare the first commit
* **Note**: This is the opposite of the order used in `git diff`.

#### Comparison to patches

While similar to patches, diffs:

* Don't have a commit header (username, commit message, etc)
* Support the optional `path=foo/bar.py` query param to filter
  the diff to just that one file diff

#### Response

The raw diff is returned as-is, in whatever encoding the files in the
repository use. It is not decoded into unicode. As such, the
content-type is `text/plain`.

<h3 id="compare-two-commits-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|context|query|integer|false|Generate diffs with <n> lines of context instead of the usual three.|
|path|query|string|false|Limit the diff to a particular file (this parameter<br>can be repeated for multiple paths).|
|ignore_whitespace|query|boolean|false|Generate diffs that ignore whitespace.|
|binary|query|boolean|false|Generate diffs that include binary files, true if omitted.|
|renames|query|boolean|false|Whether to perform rename detection, true if omitted.|
|merge|query|boolean|false|This parameter is deprecated. The 'topic' parameter should be used<br>instead. The 'merge' and 'topic' parameters cannot be both used at<br>the same time.<br><br>If true, the source commit is merged into the<br>destination commit, and then a diff from the<br>destination to the merge result is returned. If false,<br>a simple 'two dot' diff between the source and<br>destination is returned. True if omitted.|
|topic|query|boolean|false|If true, returns 2-way 'three-dot' diff.<br>This is a diff between the source commit and the merge base<br>of the source commit and the destination commit.<br>If false, a simple 'two dot' diff between the source and<br>destination is returned.<br><br>If omitted, defaults to true, ie. a 2 way 'three-dot'<br>diff is returned.<br>|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|spec|path|string|true|A commit SHA (e.g. `3a8b42`) or a commit range using double dot<br>notation (e.g. `3a8b42..9ff173`).<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

```json
  "type": "string",
  "error": {

    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

|200|OK|The raw diff|None|
|555|555|If the diff was too large and timed out.<br><br>Since this endpoint does not employ any form of pagination, but<br>instead returns the diff as a single document, it can run into<br>trouble on very large diffs. If Bitbucket times out in cases<br>like these, a 555 status code is returned.|[error](#schemaerror)|

## Compare two commit diff stats

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/diffstat/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/diffstat/{spec}`

Produces a response in JSON format with a record for every path
modified, including information on the type of the change and the
number of lines added and removed.

#### Single commit spec

If the `spec` argument to this API is a single commit, the diff is
produced against the first parent of the specified commit.

#### Two commit spec

Two commits separated by `..` may be provided as the `spec`, e.g.,
`3a8b42..9ff173`. When two commits are provided and the `topic` query
parameter is true, this API produces a 2-way three dot diff.
This is the diff between source commit and the merge base of the source
commit and the destination commit. When the `topic` query param is false,
a simple git-style diff is produced.

The two commits are interpreted as follows:

* First commit: the commit containing the changes we wish to preview
* Second commit: the commit representing the state to which we want to
  compare the first commit
* **Note**: This is the opposite of the order used in `git diff`.

<h3 id="compare-two-commit-diff-stats-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ignore_whitespace|query|boolean|false|Generate diffs that ignore whitespace|
|merge|query|boolean|false|This parameter is deprecated. The 'topic' parameter should be used<br>instead. The 'merge' and 'topic' parameters cannot be both used at<br>the same time.<br><br>If true, the source commit is merged into the<br>destination commit, and then a diffstat from the<br>destination to the merge result is returned. If false,<br>a simple 'two dot' diffstat between the source and<br>destination is returned. True if omitted.|
|path|query|string|false|Limit the diffstat to a particular file (this parameter<br>can be repeated for multiple paths).|
|renames|query|boolean|false|Whether to perform rename detection, true if omitted.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|spec|path|string|true|A commit SHA (e.g. `3a8b42`) or a commit range using double dot<br>notation (e.g. `3a8b42..9ff173`).<br>|
|topic|query|boolean|false|If true, returns 2-way 'three-dot' diff.<br>This is a diff between the source commit and the merge base<br>of the source commit and the destination commit.<br>If false, a simple 'two dot' diff between the source and<br>destination is returned.|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "pagelen": 500,
  "values": [
    {
      "type": "diffstat",
      "status": "modified",
      "lines_removed": 1,
      "lines_added": 2,
      "old": {
        "path": "setup.py",
        "escaped_path": "setup.py",
        "type": "commit_file",
        "links": {
          "self": {
            "href": "https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/bitbucket/geordi/src/e1749643d655d7c7014001a6c0f58abaf42ad850/setup.py"
          }
        }
      },
      "new": {
        "path": "setup.py",
        "escaped_path": "setup.py",
        "type": "commit_file",
        "links": {
          "self": {
            "href": "https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/bitbucket/geordi/src/d222fa235229c55dad20b190b0b571adf737d5a6/setup.py"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "page": 1,
  "size": 1
}
```

> 555 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="compare-two-commit-diff-stats-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The diff stats|[paginated_diffstats](#schemapaginated_diffstats)|
|555|555|If generating the diffstat timed out.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: repository ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## Get a patch for two commits

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/patch/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/patch/{spec}`

Produces a raw patch for a single commit (diffed against its first
parent), or a patch-series for a revspec of 2 commits (e.g.
`3a8b42..9ff173` where the first commit represents the source and the
second commit the destination).

In case of the latter (diffing a revspec), a patch series is returned
for the commits on the source branch (`3a8b42` and its ancestors in
our example).

While similar to diffs, patches:

* Have a commit header (username, commit message, etc)
* Do not support the `path=foo/bar.py` query parameter

The raw patch is returned as-is, in whatever encoding the files in the
repository use. It is not decoded into unicode. As such, the
content-type is `text/plain`.

<h3 id="get-a-patch-for-two-commits-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|spec|path|string|true|A commit SHA (e.g. `3a8b42`) or a commit range using double dot<br>notation (e.g. `3a8b42..9ff173`).<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 555 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-a-patch-for-two-commits-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The raw patches|None|
|555|555|If the diff was too large and timed out.<br><br>Since this endpoint does not employ any form of pagination, but<br>instead returns the diff as a single document, it can run into<br>trouble on very large diffs. If Bitbucket times out in cases<br>like these, a 555 status code is returned.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: repository ), basic, api_key
</aside>

<h1 id="bitbucket-api-deployments">Deployments</h1>

Teams are deploying code faster than ever, thanks to continuous
delivery practices and tools like Bitbucket Pipelines. Bitbucket
Deployments gives teams visibility into their deployment
environments and helps teams to track how far changes have
progressed in their deployment pipeline.

> Code samples

```bash

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/deploy-keys`

Create a new deploy key in a repository. Note: If authenticating a deploy key
with an OAuth consumer, any changes to the OAuth consumer will subsequently
invalidate the deploy key.

```
'{
```

<h1 id="bitbucket-api-downloads">Downloads</h1>

Access the list of download links associated with the repository.

## List download artifacts

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/downloads \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/downloads`

Returns a list of download links associated with the repository.

<h3 id="list-download-artifacts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="list-download-artifacts-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns a paginated list of the downloads associated with the repository.|None|
|403|Forbidden|User is not authorized to read from the repository.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: repository ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## Upload a download artifact

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/downloads \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/downloads`

Upload new download artifacts.

To upload files, perform a `multipart/form-data` POST containing one
or more `files` fields:

    $ echo Hello World > hello.txt
    $ curl -s -u evzijst -X POST https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/evzijst/git-tests/downloads -F files=@hello.txt

When a file is uploaded with the same name as an existing artifact,
then the existing file will be replaced.

<h3 id="upload-a-download-artifact-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

> 406 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="upload-a-download-artifact-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|The artifact was uploaded sucessfully.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|403|Forbidden|User is not authorized to write to the repository.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|406|Not Acceptable|Unsupported Content-Type. Use multiplart/form-data.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: repository:write ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## Get a download artifact link

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/downloads/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/downloads/{filename}`

Return a redirect to the contents of a download artifact.

This endpoint returns the actual file contents and not the artifact's
metadata.

    $ curl -s -L https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/evzijst/git-tests/downloads/hello.txt
    Hello World

<h3 id="get-a-download-artifact-link-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filename|path|string|true|Name of the file.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-a-download-artifact-link-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|302|Found|Redirects to the url of the specified download artifact.|None|
|403|Forbidden|User is not authorized to read from the repository.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|The specified download artifact does not exist.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: repository ), basic, api_key
</aside>

|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="delete-a-download-artifact-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

oauth2 ( Scopes: repository:write ), basic, api_key

<h1 id="bitbucket-api-gpg">GPG</h1>

The GPG resource allows you to manage GPG keys.


## List GPG keys

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/users/string/gpg-keys \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /users/{selected_user}/gpg-keys`

Returns a paginated list of the user's GPG public keys.
The `key` and `subkeys` fields can also be requested from the endpoint.
See [Partial Responses](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/intro/#partial-response) for more details.

<h3 id="list-gpg-keys-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|selected_user|path|string|true|This can either be an Atlassian Account ID OR the UUID of the account,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{account UUID}`.<br>|

## Add a new GPG key

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/users/string/gpg-keys \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "string",
    "owner": {
      "type": "string",
      "links": {
        "avatar": {
          "href": "http://example.com",
          "name": "string"
        }
      },
      "created_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "display_name": "string",
      "uuid": "string"
    },
    "key": "string",
    "key_id": "string",
    "fingerprint": "string",
    "parent_fingerprint": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "expires_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "created_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "added_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "last_used": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "subkeys": [
      {}
    ],
    "links": {
      "self": {
        "href": "http://example.com",
        "name": "string"
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /users/{selected_user}/gpg-keys`

Adds a new GPG public key to the specified user account and returns the resulting key.

Example:

```
$ curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d
'{"key": "<insert GPG Key>"}'
https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/users/{d7dd0e2d-3994-4a50-a9ee-d260b6cefdab}/gpg-keys
```

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "string",

    "links": {

        "href": "http://example.com",

    "uuid": "string"

    }
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|selected_user|path|string|true|This can either be an Atlassian Account ID OR the UUID of the account,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{account UUID}`.<br>|
|body|body|[GPG_account_key](#schemagpg_account_key)|false|The new GPG key object.|
|» type|body|string|true|none|
|» owner|body|[account](#schemaaccount)|false|none|

|» fingerprint|body|string|false|The GPG key fingerprint.|
|» parent_fingerprint|body|string|false|The fingerprint of the parent key. This value is null unless the current key is a subkey.|
|» name|body|string|false|The user-defined label for the GPG key|
|» expires_on|body|string(date-time)|false|none|
|» created_on|body|string(date-time)|false|none|
|» added_on|body|string(date-time)|false|none|
|» last_used|body|string(date-time)|false|none|
|» subkeys|body|[[GPG_account_key](#schemagpg_account_key)]|false|none|
|» links|body|object|false|none|
|» » self|body|object|false|A link to a resource related to this object.|
|» » » href|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » » name|body|string|false|none|

<h1 id="bitbucket-api-merge-queues">Merge queues</h1>

Merge queues help keep a branch healthy by merging pull requests in
order, only after each one has been validated with Bitbucket
Pipelines against the latest state of the branch. When a pull
request targeting a branch with an active merge queue is merged, it
is added to the queue instead of being merged immediately.

The merge queues resource lets you list the merge queues configured
for a repository, inspect the pull requests currently in a queue,
and remove a pull request from a queue.


## List merge queues

<a id="opIdlistMergeQueues"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/merge-queues \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/merge-queues`

Lists merge queues configured for a repository. Optionally filter by branch.

<h3 id="list-merge-queues-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|The workspace containing the repository.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|The repository slug.|
|target_branch|query|string|false|Optional target branch name to filter merge queues.|
|page|query|integer(int32)|false|The page number of elements to retrieve.|
|pagelen|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of results to return.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "page": 0,
  "size": 0,
  "pagelen": 0,
  "values": [
    {
      "type": "string",
      "uuid": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "state": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json

    "data": {}
  }

```

> 404 Response

|404|Not Found|The repository does not exist.|[error](#schemaerror)|

oauth2 ( Scopes: repository ), basic, api_key
</aside>

<h3 id="get-a-pullrequest-in-a-merge-queue-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Merge queue pullrequest retrieved successfully.|[merge_queue_pullrequest](#schemamerge_queue_pullrequest)|
|400|Bad Request|The merge queue UUID is invalid.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication is required.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|403|Forbidden|The caller does not have read access to the pullrequest.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|The repository, merge queue, or pullrequest does not exist, or the pullrequest is no longer in the merge queue.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pullrequest ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## Remove a pullrequest from a merge queue

<a id="opIdremovePullRequestFromMergeQueue"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/merge-queues/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/queue/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/merge-queues/{merge_queue_uuid}/queue/{pullrequest_id}`

Removes a pullrequest from the specified merge queue asynchronously.

<h3 id="remove-a-pullrequest-from-a-merge-queue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|The workspace containing the repository.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|The repository slug.|
|merge_queue_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|The UUID of the merge queue.|
|pullrequest_id|path|integer|true|The ID of the pullrequest to remove.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {

    "data": {}
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {

    "data": {}
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="remove-a-pullrequest-from-a-merge-queue-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|The remove request was accepted.|None|
|400|Bad Request|The merge queue UUID is invalid.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication is required.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|403|Forbidden|The caller does not have write access to the pullrequest.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|The repository, merge queue, or pullrequest does not exist.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pullrequest:write ), basic, api_key
</aside>

<h1 id="bitbucket-api-pipelines">Pipelines</h1>

Bitbucket Pipelines brings continuous delivery to Bitbucket
Cloud, empowering teams with full branching to deployment
visibility and faster feedback loops.


## List variables for an environment

<a id="opIdgetDeploymentVariables"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/deployments_config/environments/string/variables \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/deployments_config/environments/{environment_uuid}/variables`

Find deployment environment level variables.

<h3 id="list-variables-for-an-environment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID surrounded by curly-braces, for example `{workspace UUID}`.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|The repository.|
|environment_uuid|path|string|true|The environment.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "page": 0,
  "values": [
    {
      "type": "string",
      "uuid": "string",
      "key": "string",
      "value": "string",
      "secured": true
    }
  ],
  "size": 0,
  "pagelen": 0,
  "next": "http://example.com",
  "previous": "http://example.com"
}
```

<h3 id="list-variables-for-an-environment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The retrieved deployment variables.|[paginated_deployment_variable](#schemapaginated_deployment_variable)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pipeline ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## Create a variable for an environment

<a id="opIdcreateDeploymentVariable"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/deployments_config/environments/string/variables \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "string",
    "uuid": "string",
    "key": "string",
    "value": "string",
    "secured": true
  }'
```

`POST /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/deployments_config/environments/{environment_uuid}/variables`

Create a deployment environment level variable.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "uuid": "string",
  "key": "string",
  "value": "string",
  "secured": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-variable-for-an-environment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID surrounded by curly-braces, for example `{workspace UUID}`.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|The repository.|
|environment_uuid|path|string|true|The environment.|
|body|body|[deployment_variable](#schemadeployment_variable)|true|The variable to create|
|» type|body|string|true|none|
|» uuid|body|string|false|The UUID identifying the variable.|
|» key|body|string|false|The unique name of the variable.|
|» value|body|string|false|The value of the variable. If the variable is secured, this will be empty.|
|» secured|body|boolean|false|If true, this variable will be treated as secured. The value will never be exposed in the logs or the REST API.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "uuid": "string",
  "key": "string",
  "value": "string",
  "secured": true
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-variable-for-an-environment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|The variable was created.|[deployment_variable](#schemadeployment_variable)|
|404|Not Found|The account, repository, environment or variable with the given UUID was not found.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|409|Conflict|A variable with the provided key already exists.|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|201|Location|string||The URL of the newly created variable.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pipeline:variable ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## Update a variable for an environment

<a id="opIdupdateDeploymentVariable"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/deployments_config/environments/string/variables/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "string",
    "uuid": "string",
    "key": "string",
    "value": "string",
    "secured": true
  }'
```

`PUT /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/deployments_config/environments/{environment_uuid}/variables/{variable_uuid}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "string",
```

|repo_slug|path|string|true|The repository.|
|environment_uuid|path|string|true|The environment.|
|variable_uuid|path|string|true|The UUID of the variable to update.|
|body|body|[deployment_variable](#schemadeployment_variable)|true|The updated deployment variable.|
|» type|body|string|true|none|
|» uuid|body|string|false|The UUID identifying the variable.|
|» key|body|string|false|The unique name of the variable.|

|» secured|body|boolean|false|If true, this variable will be treated as secured. The value will never be exposed in the logs or the REST API.|

```json
{
```
