`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pipelines`

Find pipelines in a repository.

Note that unlike other endpoints in the Bitbucket API, this endpoint utilizes query parameters to allow filtering
and sorting of returned results. See [query parameters](#api-repositories-workspace-repo-slug-pipelines-get-request-Query%20parameters)
for specific details.


<h3 id="list-pipelines-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID surrounded by curly-braces, for example `{workspace UUID}`.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|The repository.|
|creator.uuid|query|string(uuid)|false|The UUID of the creator of the pipeline to filter by.|
|target.ref_type|query|string|false|The type of the reference to filter by.|
|target.ref_name|query|string|false|The reference name to filter by.|
|target.branch|query|string|false|The name of the branch to filter by.|
|target.commit.hash|query|string|false|The revision to filter by.|
|target.selector.pattern|query|string|false|The pipeline pattern to filter by.|
|target.selector.type|query|string|false|The type of pipeline to filter by.|
|created_on|query|string(date-time)|false|The creation date to filter by.|
|trigger_type|query|string|false|The trigger type to filter by.|
|status|query|string|false|The pipeline status to filter by.|
|sort|query|string|false|The attribute name to sort on.|
|page|query|integer(int32)|false|The page number of elements to retrieve.|
|pagelen|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of results to return.|

`POST /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pipelines`

Endpoint to create and initiate a pipeline.
There are a number of different options to initiate a pipeline, where the payload of the request will determine which type of pipeline will be instantiated.

## Trigger a pipeline for a branch

One way to trigger pipelines is by specifying the branch for which you want to trigger a pipeline.
The specified branch will be used to determine which pipeline definition from the `bitbucket-pipelines.yml` file will be applied to initiate the pipeline. The pipeline will then do a clone of the repository and checkout the latest revision of the specified branch.

### Example

```
$ curl -X POST -is -u '{atlassian_account_email}:{api_token}' \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pipelines/ \
      -d '
      {
        "target": {
          "ref_type": "branch",
          "type": "pipeline_ref_target",
          "ref_name": "master"
        }
      }'
```

## Trigger a pipeline for a commit on a branch or tag

You can initiate a pipeline for a specific commit and in the context of a specified reference (e.g. a branch, tag or bookmark).
The specified reference will be used to determine which pipeline definition from the bitbucket-pipelines.yml file will be applied to initiate the pipeline. The pipeline will clone the repository and then do a checkout the specified reference.

The following reference types are supported:

* `branch`
* `named_branch`
* `bookmark`
 * `tag`

### Example

```
$ curl -X POST -is -u '{atlassian_account_email}:{api_token}' \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pipelines/ \
      -d '
      {
        "target": {
          "commit": {
            "type": "commit",
            "hash": "ce5b7431602f7cbba007062eeb55225c6e18e956"
          },
          "ref_type": "branch",
          "type": "pipeline_ref_target",
          "ref_name": "master"
        }
      }'
```

## Trigger a specific pipeline definition for a commit

You can trigger a specific pipeline that is defined in your `bitbucket-pipelines.yml` file for a specific commit.
In addition to the commit revision, you specify the type and pattern of the selector that identifies the pipeline definition. The resulting pipeline will then clone the repository and checkout the specified revision.

### Example

```
$ curl -X POST -is -u '{atlassian_account_email}:{api_token}' \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pipelines/ \
      -d '
      {
        "target": {
          "commit": {
            "hash":"a3c4e02c9a3755eccdc3764e6ea13facdf30f923",
            "type":"commit"
          },
          "selector": {
            "type":"custom",
            "pattern":"Deploy to production"
          },
          "type":"pipeline_commit_target"
        }
      }'
```

## Trigger a specific pipeline definition for a commit on a branch or tag

You can trigger a specific pipeline that is defined in your `bitbucket-pipelines.yml` file for a specific commit in the context of a specified reference.
In addition to the commit revision, you specify the type and pattern of the selector that identifies the pipeline definition, as well as the reference information. The resulting pipeline will then clone the repository a checkout the specified reference.

### Example

```
$ curl -X POST -is -u '{atlassian_account_email}:{api_token}' \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pipelines/ \
      -d '
      {
        "target": {
          "commit": {
            "hash":"a3c4e02c9a3755eccdc3764e6ea13facdf30f923",
            "type":"commit"
          },
          "selector": {
            "type": "custom",
            "pattern": "Deploy to production"
          },
          "type": "pipeline_ref_target",
          "ref_name": "master",
          "ref_type": "branch"
        }
      }'
```

## Trigger a custom pipeline with variables

In addition to triggering a custom pipeline that is defined in your `bitbucket-pipelines.yml` file as shown in the examples above, you can specify variables that will be available for your build. In the request, provide a list of variables, specifying the following for each variable: key, value, and whether it should be secured or not (this field is optional and defaults to not secured).

### Example

```
$ curl -X POST -is -u '{atlassian_account_email}:{api_token}' \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pipelines/ \
      -d '
      {
        "target": {
          "type": "pipeline_ref_target",
          "ref_type": "branch",
          "ref_name": "master",
          "selector": {
            "type": "custom",
            "pattern": "Deploy to production"
          }
        },
        "variables": [
          {
            "key": "var1key",
            "value": "var1value",
            "secured": true
          },
          {
            "key": "var2key",
            "value": "var2value"
          }
        ]
      }'
```

## Trigger a pull request pipeline

You can also initiate a pipeline for a specific pull request.

### Example

```
$ curl -X POST -is -u '{atlassian_account_email}:{api_token}' \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pipelines/ \
      -d '
      {
        "target": {
          "type": "pipeline_pullrequest_target",
          "source": "pull-request-branch",
          "destination": "master",
          "destination_commit": {
            "hash": "9f848b7"
          },
          "commit": {
            "hash": "1a372fc"
          },
          "pullrequest": {
            "id": "3"
          },
          "selector": {
            "type": "pull-requests",
            "pattern": "**"
          }
        }
      }'
```

# On-demand pipeline

By default, pipelines run using the YAML in the repository’s `bitbucket-pipelines.yml` configuration file.
With an _on-demand_ pipeline, you include the pipeline’s YAML in the request body. That YAML applies only
to that run and overrides the YAML in `bitbucket-pipelines.yml`.

Just like with regular pipelines, there is a number of different options to initiate an on-demand pipeline.
However, since the payload contains YAML configuration in this case, _query parameters_ are used to supply
the necessary metadata to determine which type of pipeline will be instantiated. These query parameters
are derived from the JSON equivalent by turning each property into a key-value pair with the JSON path
of the property as the new key.

## Optional on-demand query parameters

Use `merge_defaults=true` to merge repository-level defaults into the supplied YAML. Pipelines merges
`image`, `options`, `clone`, `export`, `labels`, and definitions. The supplied YAML still controls
pipeline steps.

Use `target_branch_to_create` to create a branch from the requested branch or commit target before the
run starts. Pipelines then uses the new branch as the on-demand pipeline target.

## Trigger on-demand pipeline for a branch

You can initiate an on-demand pipeline for a specific branch. This branch will be used to determine
which pipeline definition from the supplied YAML configuration will be applied to initiate the pipeline.
The pipeline will then do a clone of the repository and check out the latest revision of the specified branch.

To trigger an on-demand pipeline for a _branch_ the requesting user must have **write permission** for
that branch (which can be limited by [branch restrictions](https://support.atlassian.com/bitbucket-cloud/docs/use-branch-permissions/)).

### Example

```
$ curl -X POST -is -u '{atlassian_account_email}:{api_token}' \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/yaml' \
      https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pipelines?target.type=pipeline_ref_target&target.ref_type=branch&target.ref_name=master \
      -d '
pipelines:
  default:
    - step:
        script:
          - echo This is an on-demand pipeline'
```

## Trigger on-demand pipeline for a commit on a branch or tag

You can initiate an on-demand pipeline for a specific commit and in the context of a specified reference
(branch or tag). The specified reference will be used to determine which pipeline definition from the supplied
YAML configuration will be applied to initiate the pipeline. The pipeline will clone the repository and
check out the specified reference.

To trigger an on-demand pipeline for a _branch_ the requesting user must have **write permission** for
that branch (which can be limited by [branch restrictions](https://support.atlassian.com/bitbucket-cloud/docs/use-branch-permissions/)).

### Example

```
$ curl -X POST -is -u '{atlassian_account_email}:{api_token}' \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/yaml' \
      https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pipelines?target.type=pipeline_ref_target&target.ref_type=branch&target.ref_name=master&target.commit.hash=ce5b7431602f7cbba007062eeb55225c6e18e956 \
      -d '
pipelines:
  default:
    - step:
        script:
          - echo This is an on-demand pipeline'
```

## Trigger a specific on-demand pipeline definition for a commit

You can trigger a specific pipeline that is defined in the supplied YAML configuration for a specific commit.
In addition to the commit revision, you specify the type and pattern of the selector that identifies
the pipeline definition. The resulting pipeline will then clone the repository and checkout the specified revision.

### Example

```
$ curl -X POST -is -u '{atlassian_account_email}:{api_token}' \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/yaml' \
      https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pipelines?target.type=pipeline_commit_target&target.commit.hash=a3c4e02c9a3755eccdc3764e6ea13facdf30f923&target.selector.type=custom&target.selector.pattern=security-scan \
      -d '
pipelines:
  custom:
    security-scan:
      - step:
          script:
            - echo Run on-demand security scan
```

## Trigger a custom on-demand pipeline with variables

In addition to triggering a custom on-demand pipeline that is defined in the supplied YAML configuration
as shown in the examples above, you can specify variables that will be available for your build.
In the request, provide each variable as an indexed set of query parameters representing its key, value,
and whether it should be secured or not (this field is optional and defaults to not secured).

### Example

```
$ curl -X POST -is -u '{atlassian_account_email}:{api_token}' \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/yaml' \
      https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pipelines?target.type=pipeline_ref_target&target.ref_type=branch&target.ref_name=master&target.selector.type=custom&target.selector.pattern=security-scan&variables[0].key=var1key&variables[0].value=var1value&variables[0].secured=true&variables[1].key=var2key&variables[1].value=var2value \
      -d '
pipelines:
  custom:
    security-scan:
      - variables:
          - name: var1key
          - name: var2key
      - step:
          script:
            - echo Run on-demand security scan'
```

## Trigger a pull request pipeline

You can also initiate an on-demand pipeline for a specific pull request.

### Example

```
$ curl -X POST -is -u '{atlassian_account_email}:{api_token}' \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/yaml' \
      https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pipelines?target.type=pipeline_pullrequest_target&target.source=pull-request-branch&target.destination=destination&target.destination_commit.hash=9f848b7&target.commit.hash=1a372fc&target.pullrequest.id=3&target.selector.type=pull-requests&target.selector.pattern=** \
      -d '
pipelines:
  pull-requests:
    "**":
      - step:
          script:
            - echo This is an on-demand pipeline'
```

|» type|body|string|true|none|
|» uuid|body|string|false|The UUID identifying the pipeline.|
|» build_number|body|integer|false|The build number of the pipeline.|
|» creator|body|[account](#schemaaccount)|false|none|
|» repository|body|[repository](#schemarepository)|false|none|
|» target|body|[pipeline_target](#schemapipeline_target)|false|none|
|» trigger|body|[pipeline_trigger](#schemapipeline_trigger)|false|none|
|» state|body|[pipeline_state](#schemapipeline_state)|false|none|
|» variables|body|[[pipeline_variable](#schemapipeline_variable)]|false|The variables for the pipeline.|
|» created_on|body|string(date-time)|false|The timestamp when the pipeline was created.|
|» completed_on|body|string(date-time)|false|The timestamp when the Pipeline was completed. This is not set if the pipeline is still in progress.|
|» build_seconds_used|body|integer|false|The number of build seconds used by this pipeline.|
|» configuration_sources|body|[[pipeline_configuration_source](#schemapipeline_configuration_source)]|false|An ordered list of sources of the pipeline configuration|
|» links|body|[pipelines_pipeline_links](#schemapipelines_pipeline_links)|false|none|

## Get log file for a step

<a id="opIdgetPipelineStepLogForRepository"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/pipelines/string/steps/string/log \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pipelines/{pipeline_uuid}/steps/{step_uuid}/log`

Retrieve the log file for a given step of a pipeline.

This endpoint supports (and encourages!) the use of [HTTP Range requests](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7233) to deal with potentially very large log files.

<h3 id="get-log-file-for-a-step-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID surrounded by curly-braces, for example `{workspace UUID}`.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|The repository.|
|pipeline_uuid|path|string|true|The UUID of the pipeline.|
|step_uuid|path|string|true|The UUID of the step.|

<h3 id="get-log-file-for-a-step-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The raw log file for this pipeline step.|None|
|304|Not Modified|The log has the same etag as the provided If-None-Match header.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|307|Temporary Redirect|After the step is completed, the log is moved to long term storage and a redirection to the log file is returned.|None|
|404|Not Found|A pipeline with the given UUID does not exist, a step with the given UUID does not exist in the pipeline or a log file does not exist for the given step.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|416|Range Not Satisfiable|The requested range does not exist for requests that specified the [HTTP Range header](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7233#section-3.1).|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pipeline ), basic, api_key
</aside>

<h3 id="get-test-case-reasons-output-for-a-given-test-case-in-a-step-of-a-pipeline-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Test case reasons (output).|None|
|404|Not Found|No account, repository, pipeline, step or test case with the UUID provided exists for the pipeline with the UUID provided.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pipeline ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## Stop a pipeline

<a id="opIdstopPipeline"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/pipelines/string/stopPipeline \

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pipelines/{pipeline_uuid}/stopPipeline`

Signal the stop of a pipeline and all of its steps that not have completed yet.

<h3 id="stop-a-pipeline-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID surrounded by curly-braces, for example `{workspace UUID}`.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|The repository.|
|pipeline_uuid|path|string|true|The UUID of the pipeline.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="stop-a-pipeline-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|The pipeline has been signaled to stop.|None|
|400|Bad Request|The specified pipeline has already completed.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|Either the account, repository or pipeline with the given UUID does not exist.|[error](#schemaerror)|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pipeline:write ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## Update the next build number

<a id="opIdupdateRepositoryBuildNumber"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/pipelines_config/build_number \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "string",
    "next": 0
  }'
```

`PUT /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pipelines_config/build_number`

Update the next build number that should be assigned to a pipeline. The next build number that will be configured has to be strictly higher than the current latest build number for this repository.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "next": 0
}
```

<h3 id="update-the-next-build-number-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID surrounded by curly-braces, for example `{workspace UUID}`.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|The repository.|
|body|body|[pipeline_build_number](#schemapipeline_build_number)|true|The build number to update.|
|» type|body|string|true|none|
|» next|body|integer|false|The next number that will be used as build number.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "next": 0
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-the-next-build-number-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The build number has been configured.|[pipeline_build_number](#schemapipeline_build_number)|
|400|Bad Request|The update failed because the next number was invalid (it should be higher than the current number).|[error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|The account or repository was not found.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pipeline:variable ), basic, api_key
</aside>

<h1 id="bitbucket-api-projects">Projects</h1>

Bitbucket Cloud projects make it easier for teams to focus on
a goal, product, or process by organizing their repositories.


## Create a project in a workspace

> Code samples


`POST /workspaces/{workspace}/projects`

Creates a new project.

Note that the avatar has to be embedded as either a data-url
or a URL to an external image as shown in the examples below:

```
$ body=$(cat << EOF
{
    "name": "Mars Project",
    "key": "MARS",
    "description": "Software for colonizing mars.",
    "links": {
        "avatar": {
            "href": "data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhEAAQAMQAAORHHOVSKudfOulrSOp3WOyDZu6QdvCchPGolfO0o/..."
        }
    },
    "is_private": false
}
EOF
)
$ curl -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
       -X POST \
       -d "$body" \
       https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/workspaces/teams-in-space/projects/ | jq .
{
  // Serialized project document
}
```

or even:

```
$ body=$(cat << EOF
{
    "name": "Mars Project",
    "key": "MARS",
    "description": "Software for colonizing mars.",
    "links": {
        "avatar": {
            "href": "http://i.imgur.com/72tRx4w.gif"
        }
    },
    "is_private": false
}
EOF
)
$ curl -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
       -X POST \
       -d "$body" \
       https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/workspaces/teams-in-space/projects/ | jq .
{
  // Serialized project document
}
```

`PUT /workspaces/{workspace}/projects/{project_key}`

Since this endpoint can be used to both update and to create a
project, the request body depends on the intent.

#### Creation

See the POST documentation for the project collection for an
example of the request body.

Note: The `key` should not be specified in the body of request
(since it is already present in the URL). The `name` is required,
everything else is optional.

#### Update

See the POST documentation for the project collection for an
example of the request body.

Note: The key is not required in the body (since it is already in
the URL). The key may be specified in the body, if the intent is
to change the key itself. In such a scenario, the location of the
project is changed and is returned in the `Location` header of the
response.

## Delete a project for a workspace

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/workspaces/string/projects/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /workspaces/{workspace}/projects/{project_key}`

Deletes this project. This is an irreversible operation.

You cannot delete a project that still contains repositories.
To delete the project, [delete](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/api-group-repositories/#api-repositories-workspace-repo-slug-delete)
or transfer the repositories first.

Example:
```
$ curl -X DELETE https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/workspaces/bbworkspace1/projects/PROJ
```

<h3 id="delete-a-project-for-a-workspace-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project_key|path|string|true|The project in question. This is the actual `key` assigned<br>to the project.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="delete-a-project-for-a-workspace-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Successful deletion.|None|
|403|Forbidden|The requesting user isn't authorized to delete the project or the project isn't empty.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|A project isn't hosted at this location.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: project:admin ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## Update an explicit group permission for a project

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/workspaces/string/projects/string/permissions-config/groups/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "permission": "read"
  }'
```

`PUT /workspaces/{workspace}/projects/{project_key}/permissions-config/groups/{group_slug}`

Updates the group permission, or grants a new permission if one does not already exist.

Only users with admin permission for the project may access this resource.

Due to security concerns, the JWT and OAuth authentication methods are unsupported.
This is to ensure integrations and add-ons are not allowed to change permissions.

Permissions can be:

* `admin`

## Update an explicit user permission for a project

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/workspaces/string/projects/string/permissions-config/users/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "permission": "read"
  }'
```

`PUT /workspaces/{workspace}/projects/{project_key}/permissions-config/users/{selected_user_id}`

Updates the explicit user permission for a given user and project. The selected
user must be a member of the workspace, and cannot be the workspace owner.

Only users with admin permission for the project may access this resource.

Due to security concerns, the JWT and OAuth authentication methods are unsupported.
This is to ensure integrations and add-ons are not allowed to change permissions.

Permissions can be:

* `admin`
* `create-repo`
* `write`
* `read`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "permission": "read"
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-explicit-user-permission-for-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|selected_user_id|path|string|true|This can either be the username, the user's UUID surrounded by curly-braces,<br>for example: {account UUID}, or the user's Atlassian ID.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|
|body|body|[bitbucket.apps.permissions.serializers.ProjectPermissionUpdateSchema](#schemabitbucket.apps.permissions.serializers.projectpermissionupdateschema)|true|The permission to grant|
|» permission|body|string|true|none|

<h1 id="bitbucket-api-pullrequests">Pullrequests</h1>

Pull requests are a feature that makes it easier for developers
to collaborate using Bitbucket. They provide a user-friendly web
interface for discussing proposed changes before integrating them
into the official project.


## List pull requests that contain a commit

<a id="opIdgetPullrequestsForCommit"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/commit/string/pullrequests \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/commit/{commit}/pullrequests`

Returns a paginated list of all pull requests as part of which this commit was reviewed. Pull Request Commit Links app must be installed first before using this API; installation automatically occurs when 'Go to pull request' is clicked from the web interface for a commit's details.

<h3 id="list-pull-requests-that-contain-a-commit-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID surrounded by curly-braces|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|The repository; either the UUID in curly braces, or the slug|
|commit|path|string|true|The SHA1 of the commit|
|page|query|integer(int32)|false|Which page to retrieve|
|pagelen|query|integer(int32)|false|How many pull requests to retrieve per page|

<h3 id="list-pull-requests-that-contain-a-commit-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The paginated list of pull requests.|[paginated_pullrequests](#schemapaginated_pullrequests)|
|202|Accepted|The repository's pull requests are still being indexed.|[paginated_pullrequests](#schemapaginated_pullrequests)|
|404|Not Found|Either the repository does not exist, or pull request commit links have not yet been indexed.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pullrequest ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## List default reviewers

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/default-reviewers \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/default-reviewers`

Returns the repository's default reviewers.

These are the users that are automatically added as reviewers on every
new pull request that is created. To obtain the repository's default reviewers
as well as the default reviewers inherited from the project, use the
[effective-default-reveiwers](#api-repositories-workspace-repo-slug-effective-default-reviewers-get) endpoint.

<h3 id="list-default-reviewers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "size": 0,
  "page": 1,
  "pagelen": 1,
  "next": "http://example.com",
  "previous": "http://example.com",
  "values": [
    {
      "type": "string",
      "links": {
        "avatar": {
          "href": "http://example.com",
          "name": "string"
        }
      },
      "created_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "display_name": "string",
      "uuid": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="list-default-reviewers-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The paginated list of default reviewers|[paginated_accounts](#schemapaginated_accounts)|
|403|Forbidden|If the authenticated user does not have access to view the default reviewers|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pullrequest ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## Get a default reviewer

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/default-reviewers/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/default-reviewers/{target_username}`

Returns the specified reviewer.

This can be used to test whether a user is among the repository's
default reviewers list. A 404 indicates that that specified user is not
a default reviewer.

<h3 id="get-a-default-reviewer-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|target_username|path|string|true|This can either be the username or the UUID of the default reviewer,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{account UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "links": {
    "avatar": {
      "href": "http://example.com",
      "name": "string"
    }
  },
  "created_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "display_name": "string",
  "uuid": "string"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-a-default-reviewer-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The specified user is a default reviewer|[account](#schemaaccount)|
|403|Forbidden|If the authenticated user does not have access to check if the specified user is a default reviewer|[error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|If the specified user does not exist or is not a default reviewer|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pullrequest ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## Add a user to the default reviewers

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/default-reviewers/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`PUT /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/default-reviewers/{target_username}`

Adds the specified user to the repository's list of default
reviewers.

This method is idempotent. Adding a user a second time has no effect.

<h3 id="add-a-user-to-the-default-reviewers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|target_username|path|string|true|This can either be the username or the UUID of the default reviewer,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{account UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

## List effective default reviewers

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/effective-default-reviewers \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/effective-default-reviewers`

Returns the repository's effective default reviewers. This includes both default
reviewers defined at the repository level as well as those inherited from its project.

These are the users that are automatically added as reviewers on every
new pull request that is created.

<h3 id="list-effective-default-reviewers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

|403|Forbidden|If the authenticated user does not have access to view the default reviewers|[error](#schemaerror)|

</aside>

## List pull requests

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/pullrequests \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests`

Returns all pull requests on the specified repository.

By default only open pull requests are returned. This can be controlled
using the `state` query parameter. To retrieve pull requests that are
in one of multiple states, repeat the `state` parameter for each
individual state.

This endpoint also supports filtering and sorting of the results. See
[filtering and sorting](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/intro/#filtering) for more details.

<h3 id="list-pull-requests-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|state|query|string|false|Only return pull requests that are in this state. This parameter can be repeated.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|state|OPEN|
|state|MERGED|
|state|DECLINED|
|state|SUPERSEDED|

`POST /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests`

Creates a new pull request where the destination repository is
this repository and the author is the authenticated user.

The minimum required fields to create a pull request are `title` and
`source`, specified by a branch name.

```
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/my-workspace/my-repository/pullrequests \
    -u my-username:my-password \
    --request POST \
    --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --data '{
        "title": "My Title",
        "source": {
            "branch": {
                "name": "staging"
            }
        }
    }'
```

If the pull request's `destination` is not specified, it will default
to the `repository.mainbranch`. To open a pull request to a
different branch, say from a feature branch to a staging branch,
specify a `destination` (same format as the `source`):

```
{
    "title": "My Title",
    "source": {
        "branch": {
            "name": "my-feature-branch"
        }
    },
    "destination": {
        "branch": {
            "name": "staging"
        }
    }
}
```

Reviewers can be specified by adding an array of user objects as the
`reviewers` property.

```
{
    "title": "My Title",
    "source": {
        "branch": {
            "name": "my-feature-branch"
        }
    },
    "reviewers": [
        {
            "uuid": "{504c3b62-8120-4f0c-a7bc-87800b9d6f70}"
        }
    ]
}
```

Other fields:

* `description` - a string
* `close_source_branch` - boolean that specifies if the source branch should be closed upon merging
* `draft` - boolean that specifies whether the pull request is a draft

<h3 id="create-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|
|body|body|[pullrequest](#schemapullrequest)|false|The new pull request.<br><br>The request URL you POST to becomes the destination repository URL. For this reason, you must specify an explicit source repository in the request object if you want to pull from a different repository (fork).<br><br>Since not all elements are required or even mutable, you only need to include the elements you want to initialize, such as the source branch and the title.|

|» created_on|body|string(date-time)|false|The ISO8601 timestamp the request was created.|
|» updated_on|body|string(date-time)|false|The ISO8601 timestamp the request was last updated.|
|» reviewers|body|[[account](#schemaaccount)]|false|The list of users that were added as reviewers on this pull request when it was created. For performance reasons, the API only includes this list on a pull request's `self` URL.|
|» participants|body|[[participant](#schemaparticipant)]|false|        The list of users that are collaborating on this pull request.<br>        Collaborators are user that:<br><br>        * are added to the pull request as a reviewer (part of the reviewers<br>          list)<br>        * are not explicit reviewers, but have commented on the pull request<br>        * are not explicit reviewers, but have approved the pull request<br><br>        Each user is wrapped in an object that indicates the user's role and<br>        whether they have approved the pull request. For performance reasons,<br>        the API only returns this list when an API requests a pull request by<br>        id.<br>        |
|» draft|body|boolean|false|A boolean flag indicating whether the pull request is a draft.|
|» queued|body|boolean|false|A boolean flag indicating whether the pull request is queued|

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pullrequest:write ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## List a pull request activity log

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/pullrequests/activity \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/activity`

Returns a paginated list of the pull request's activity log.

This handler serves both a v20 and internal endpoint. The v20 endpoint
returns reviewer comments, updates, approvals and request changes. The internal
endpoint includes those plus tasks and attachments.

Comments created on a file or a line of code have an inline property.

<h3 id="list-a-pull-request-activity-log-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

## Get a pull request

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/pullrequests/0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/{pull_request_id}`

Returns the specified pull request.

<h3 id="get-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pull_request_id|path|integer|true|The id of the pull request.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

<h3 id="get-a-pull-request-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The pull request object|[pullrequest](#schemapullrequest)|
|401|Unauthorized|If the repository is private and the request was not authenticated.|None|
|404|Not Found|If the repository or pull request does not exist|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pullrequest ), basic, api_key
</aside>

`PUT /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/{pull_request_id}`

Mutates the specified pull request.

This can be used to change the pull request's branches or description.

Only open pull requests can be mutated.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "links": {
    "self": {
      "href": "http://example.com",
      "name": "string"
    },
    "html": {
      "href": "http://example.com",
      "name": "string"
    },
    "commits": {
      "href": "http://example.com",
      "name": "string"
    },
    "approve": {
      "href": "http://example.com",
      "name": "string"
    },
```

|pull_request_id|path|integer|true|The id of the pull request.|

|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|
|body|body|[pullrequest](#schemapullrequest)|false|The pull request that is to be updated.|

|» task_count|body|integer|false|The number of open tasks for a specific pull request.|
|» close_source_branch|body|boolean|false|A boolean flag indicating if merging the pull request closes the source branch.|
|» closed_by|body|[account](#schemaaccount)|false|none|
|» reason|body|string|false|Explains why a pull request was declined. This field is only applicable to pull requests in rejected state.|
|» created_on|body|string(date-time)|false|The ISO8601 timestamp the request was created.|
|» updated_on|body|string(date-time)|false|The ISO8601 timestamp the request was last updated.|
|» reviewers|body|[[account](#schemaaccount)]|false|The list of users that were added as reviewers on this pull request when it was created. For performance reasons, the API only includes this list on a pull request's `self` URL.|
|» participants|body|[[participant](#schemaparticipant)]|false|        The list of users that are collaborating on this pull request.<br>        Collaborators are user that:<br><br>        * are added to the pull request as a reviewer (part of the reviewers<br>          list)<br>        * are not explicit reviewers, but have commented on the pull request<br>        * are not explicit reviewers, but have approved the pull request<br><br>        Each user is wrapped in an object that indicates the user's role and<br>        whether they have approved the pull request. For performance reasons,<br>        the API only returns this list when an API requests a pull request by<br>        id.<br>        |
|» draft|body|boolean|false|A boolean flag indicating whether the pull request is a draft.|
|» queued|body|boolean|false|A boolean flag indicating whether the pull request is queued|

## List a pull request activity log

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/pullrequests/0/activity \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/{pull_request_id}/activity`

Returns a paginated list of the pull request's activity log.

This handler serves both a v20 and internal endpoint. The v20 endpoint
returns reviewer comments, updates, approvals and request changes. The internal
endpoint includes those plus tasks and attachments.

Comments created on a file or a line of code have an inline property.

## Approve a pull request

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/pullrequests/0/approve \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/{pull_request_id}/approve`

Approve the specified pull request as the authenticated user.

<h3 id="approve-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pull_request_id|path|integer|true|The id of the pull request.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The `participant` object recording that the authenticated user approved the pull request.|[participant](#schemaparticipant)|
|401|Unauthorized|The request wasn't authenticated.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">

oauth2 ( Scopes: pullrequest:write ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## Unapprove a pull request

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/pullrequests/0/approve \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/{pull_request_id}/approve`

Redact the authenticated user's approval of the specified pull
request.

<h3 id="unapprove-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|pull_request_id|path|integer|true|The id of the pull request.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

> Example responses

```json
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="unapprove-a-pull-request-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|An empty response indicating the authenticated user's approval has been withdrawn.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Pull request cannot be unapproved because the pull request has already been merged.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|The request wasn't authenticated.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|The specified pull request or the repository does not exist.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pullrequest:write ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## List comments on a pull request

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/pullrequests/0/comments \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/{pull_request_id}/comments`

Returns a paginated list of the pull request's comments.

This includes both global, inline comments and replies.

The default sorting is oldest to newest and can be overridden with
the `sort` query parameter.

This endpoint also supports filtering and sorting of the results. See
[filtering and sorting](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/intro/#filtering) for more
details.

<h3 id="list-comments-on-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pull_request_id|path|integer|true|The id of the pull request.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

<h3 id="list-comments-on-a-pull-request-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|A paginated list of comments made on the given pull request, in chronological order.|[paginated_pullrequest_comments](#schemapaginated_pullrequest_comments)|
|403|Forbidden|If the authenticated user does not have access to the pull request.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|If the pull request does not exist.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pullrequest ), basic, api_key
</aside>

`POST /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/{pull_request_id}/comments`

<h3 id="create-a-comment-on-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pull_request_id|path|integer|true|The id of the pull request.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|
|body|body|[pullrequest_comment](#schemapullrequest_comment)|true|The comment object.|
|» type|body|string|true|none|
|» id|body|integer(int64)|false|none|
|» created_on|body|string(date-time)|false|none|
|» updated_on|body|string(date-time)|false|none|
|» content|body|object|false|none|
|» » raw|body|string|false|The text as it was typed by a user.|
|» » markup|body|string|false|The type of markup language the raw content is to be interpreted in.|
|» » html|body|string|false|The user's content rendered as HTML.|
|» user|body|[account](#schemaaccount)|false|none|
|» deleted|body|boolean|false|none|
|» parent|body|[comment](#schemacomment)|false|none|
|» inline|body|object|false|none|
|» » from|body|integer|false|The comment's anchor line in the old version of the file. If the comment is a multi-line comment, this is the ending line number in the old version of the file.|
|» » to|body|integer|false|The comment's anchor line in the new version of the file. If the comment is a multi-line comment, this is the ending line number in the new version of the file.|
|» » start_from|body|integer|false|The starting line number in the old version of the file, if the comment is a multi-line comment. This is null otherwise.|
|» » start_to|body|integer|false|The starting line number in the new version of the file, if the comment is a multi-line comment. This is null otherwise.|
|» » path|body|string|true|The path of the file this comment is anchored to.|
|» links|body|object|false|none|
|» » self|body|object|false|A link to a resource related to this object.|
|» » » href|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» » html|body|object|false|A link to a resource related to this object.|
|» » » href|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» » code|body|object|false|A link to a resource related to this object.|
|» » » href|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» pullrequest|body|[pullrequest](#schemapullrequest)|false|none|
|» resolution|body|[comment_resolution](#schemacomment_resolution)|false|The resolution object for a Comment.|
|» pending|body|boolean|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » markup|markdown|
|» » markup|creole|
|» » markup|plaintext|

<h3 id="create-a-comment-on-a-pull-request-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|The newly created comment.|[pullrequest_comment](#schemapullrequest_comment)|
|403|Forbidden|If the authenticated user does not have access to the pull request.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|If the pull request does not exist.|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|201|Location|string||The URL of the new comment|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pullrequest ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## Get a comment on a pull request

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/pullrequests/0/comments/0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/{pull_request_id}/comments/{comment_id}`

Returns a specific pull request comment.

<h3 id="get-a-comment-on-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|comment_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The id of the comment.|
|pull_request_id|path|integer|true|The id of the pull request.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

<h3 id="update-a-comment-on-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|comment_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The id of the comment.|
|pull_request_id|path|integer|true|The id of the pull request.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|
|body|body|[pullrequest_comment](#schemapullrequest_comment)|true|The contents of the updated comment.|
|» type|body|string|true|none|
|» id|body|integer(int64)|false|none|
|» created_on|body|string(date-time)|false|none|
|» updated_on|body|string(date-time)|false|none|
|» content|body|object|false|none|
|» » raw|body|string|false|The text as it was typed by a user.|
|» » markup|body|string|false|The type of markup language the raw content is to be interpreted in.|
|» » html|body|string|false|The user's content rendered as HTML.|
|» user|body|[account](#schemaaccount)|false|none|
|» deleted|body|boolean|false|none|
|» parent|body|[comment](#schemacomment)|false|none|
|» inline|body|object|false|none|
|» » from|body|integer|false|The comment's anchor line in the old version of the file. If the comment is a multi-line comment, this is the ending line number in the old version of the file.|
|» » to|body|integer|false|The comment's anchor line in the new version of the file. If the comment is a multi-line comment, this is the ending line number in the new version of the file.|
|» » start_from|body|integer|false|The starting line number in the old version of the file, if the comment is a multi-line comment. This is null otherwise.|
|» » start_to|body|integer|false|The starting line number in the new version of the file, if the comment is a multi-line comment. This is null otherwise.|
|» » path|body|string|true|The path of the file this comment is anchored to.|
|» links|body|object|false|none|
|» » self|body|object|false|A link to a resource related to this object.|
|» » » href|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» » html|body|object|false|A link to a resource related to this object.|
|» » » href|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» » code|body|object|false|A link to a resource related to this object.|
|» » » href|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» pullrequest|body|[pullrequest](#schemapullrequest)|false|none|
|» resolution|body|[comment_resolution](#schemacomment_resolution)|false|The resolution object for a Comment.|
|» pending|body|boolean|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » markup|markdown|
|» » markup|creole|
|» » markup|plaintext|

## Delete a comment on a pull request

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/pullrequests/0/comments/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/{pull_request_id}/comments/{comment_id}`

Deletes a specific pull request comment.

<h3 id="delete-a-comment-on-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|comment_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The id of the comment.|
|pull_request_id|path|integer|true|The id of the pull request.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="delete-a-comment-on-a-pull-request-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Successful deletion.|None|
|403|Forbidden|If the authenticated user does not have access to delete the comment.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|If the comment does not exist.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pullrequest ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## List commits on a pull request

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/pullrequests/0/commits \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/{pull_request_id}/commits`

Returns a paginated list of the pull request's commits.

These are the commits that are being merged into the destination
branch when the pull requests gets accepted.

<h3 id="list-commits-on-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pull_request_id|path|integer|true|The id of the pull request.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="list-commits-on-a-pull-request-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|A paginated list of commits made on the given pull request, in chronological order. This list will be empty if the source branch no longer exists.|None|
|403|Forbidden|If the authenticated user does not have access to the pull request.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|If the pull request does not exist or the source branch is from a forked repository which no longer exists.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pullrequest ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## Get file conflicts for a pull request

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/pullrequests/0/conflicts \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/{pull_request_id}/conflicts`

Redirects to the [repository file conflicts](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/api-group-commits/#api-repositories-workspace-repo-slug-file-conflicts-spec-get)
with the revspec that corresponds to the pull request.

<h3 id="get-file-conflicts-for-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pull_request_id|path|integer|true|The id of the pull request.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

<h3 id="get-file-conflicts-for-a-pull-request-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|302|Found|Redirects to the [repository file conflicts](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/api-group-commits/#api-repositories-workspace-repo-slug-file-conflicts-spec-get) with the<br>revspec that corresponds to the pull request.<br>|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pullrequest ), basic, api_key
</aside>

<h3 id="decline-a-pull-request-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The pull request was successfully declined.|[pullrequest](#schemapullrequest)|
|555|555|If the decline took too long and timed out.<br>In this case the caller should retry the request later.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pullrequest:write ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## List changes in a pull request

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/pullrequests/0/diff \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/{pull_request_id}/diff`

Redirects to the [repository diff](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/api-group-commits/#api-repositories-workspace-repo-slug-diff-spec-get)
with the revspec that corresponds to the pull request.

<h3 id="list-changes-in-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pull_request_id|path|integer|true|The id of the pull request.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

<h3 id="list-changes-in-a-pull-request-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|302|Found|Redirects to the [repository diff](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/api-group-commits/#api-repositories-workspace-repo-slug-diff-spec-get) with the<br>revspec that corresponds to the pull request.<br>|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pullrequest ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## Get the diff stat for a pull request

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/pullrequests/0/diffstat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/{pull_request_id}/diffstat`

Redirects to the [repository diffstat](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/api-group-commits/#api-repositories-workspace-repo-slug-diffstat-spec-get)
with the revspec that corresponds to the pull request.

<h3 id="get-the-diff-stat-for-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pull_request_id|path|integer|true|The id of the pull request.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

<h3 id="get-the-diff-stat-for-a-pull-request-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|302|Found|Redirects to the [repository diffstat](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/api-group-commits/#api-repositories-workspace-repo-slug-diffstat-spec-get) with<br>the revspec that corresponds to pull request.<br>|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pullrequest ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## Merge a pull request

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/pullrequests/0/merge \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "string",
    "message": "string",
    "close_source_branch": true,
    "merge_strategy": "merge_commit"
  }'
```

`POST /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/{pull_request_id}/merge`

Merges the pull request.

If the destination branch has an active merge queue, the pull request
is added to the queue instead. The API returns a 202 with a polling
link to the task-status API in the Location header, even when `async`
is false. Calling it again on a queued pull request returns the same
link.

Merge queues support the `merge_commit`, `squash` and `rebase_merge`
strategies. If no strategy is given, the queue's default is used.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "close_source_branch": true,
  "merge_strategy": "merge_commit"
}
```

<h3 id="merge-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|async|query|boolean|false|Default value is false.<br><br><br>When set to true, runs merge asynchronously and<br>immediately returns a 202 with polling link to<br>the task-status API in the Location header.<br><br><br>When set to false, runs merge and waits for it to<br>complete, returning 200 when it succeeds. If the<br>duration of the merge exceeds a timeout threshold,<br>the API returns a 202 with polling link to the<br>task-status API in the Location header.|
|pull_request_id|path|integer|true|The id of the pull request.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|
|body|body|[pullrequest_merge_parameters](#schemapullrequest_merge_parameters)|false|none|
|» type|body|string|true|none|
|» message|body|string|false|The commit message that will be used on the resulting commit. Note that the size of the message is limited to 128 KiB.|
|» close_source_branch|body|boolean|false|Whether the source branch should be deleted. If this is not provided, we fallback to the value used when the pull request was created, which defaults to False|
|» merge_strategy|body|string|false|The merge strategy that will be used to merge the pull request.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» merge_strategy|merge_commit|
|» merge_strategy|squash|
|» merge_strategy|fast_forward|
|» merge_strategy|squash_fast_forward|
|» merge_strategy|rebase_fast_forward|
|» merge_strategy|rebase_merge|

## Get the merge task status for a pull request

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/pullrequests/0/merge/task-status/string \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/{pull_request_id}/merge/task-status/{task_id}`

When merging a pull request takes too long, the client receives a
task ID along with a 202 status code. The task ID can be used in a call
to this endpoint to check the status of a merge task.

```
curl -X GET https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/atlassian/bitbucket/pullrequests/2286/merge/task-status/<task_id>
```

If the merge task is not yet finished, a PENDING status will be returned.

```
HTTP/2 200
{
    "task_status": "PENDING",
    "links": {
        "self": {
            "href": "https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/atlassian/bitbucket/pullrequests/2286/merge/task-status/<task_id>"
        }
    }
}
```

If the merge was successful, a SUCCESS status will be returned.

```
HTTP/2 200
{
    "task_status": "SUCCESS",
    "links": {
        "self": {
            "href": "https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/atlassian/bitbucket/pullrequests/2286/merge/task-status/<task_id>"
        }
    },
    "merge_result": <the merged pull request object>
}
```

If the merge task failed, an error will be returned.

```
{
    "type": "error",
    "error": {
        "message": "<error message>"
    }
}
```

If the pull request was added to a merge queue, the task reports its
landing through the queue. A PENDING status is returned while it is in
the queue, with a `queued_pullrequest` object once the queue has it. A
SUCCESS status is returned once it merges, and an error if it leaves
the queue without merging. The error message can contain Markdown.

Unknown or expired task IDs return a PENDING status.

<h3 id="get-the-merge-task-status-for-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pull_request_id|path|integer|true|The id of the pull request.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|task_id|path|string|true|ID of the merge task|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

<h3 id="get-the-merge-task-status-for-a-pull-request-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns a task status if the merge is either pending or successful, and if it is successful, a pull request|None|
|400|Bad Request|If the provided task ID does not relate to this pull request, if something went wrong during the merge operation, or if the pull request left the merge queue without merging|None|
|403|Forbidden|The user making the request does not have permission to the repo and is different from the user who queued the task|None|
|409|Conflict|Unable to merge because one of the refs involved changed while attempting to merge|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pullrequest ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## List pull request mergeability checks

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/string/string/pullrequests/0/mergeability/checks \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/{pull_request_id}/mergeability/checks`

Returns the mergeability checks Bitbucket performs for this pull request, and whether each one
currently allows the pull request to be merged - simulating what the merge endpoint checks before
actually merging.

Checks cover pull request state, the current user's merge permissions, Git conflicts, configured
standard and custom merge checks, and merge queue status when available. Each check's `blocking`
attribute indicates whether it currently prevents merging. A failed check does not necessarily block a merge.

`pullrequest_state_check`, `current_user_permission_check`, and `git_mergeability_check` cover state,
permission, and Git eligibility. One `standard_merge_check` is included per configured branch/merge
restriction, and one `custom_pre_merge_check`/`custom_on_merge_check` per activated custom check - both
omitted entirely, not reported as passing, when not configured. Not exhaustive: conditions Bitbucket can't
evaluate without attempting the merge (e.g. dependency-merge requirements) aren't included. See
`PullRequestMergeabilityCheckSchema` for per-check fields, and `q` below to exclude the checks that
are expensive to evaluate.

For repositories with merge queues enabled, a `merge_queue_check` reports queue availability and
whether the pull request is already queued. It is included for open, non-draft pull requests when the
destination branch requires queueing, and for already-queued pull requests with a configured queue.
The check is omitted when no merge queue is configured for the destination branch. When the check is
present, `merge_queue` contains that configured queue's UUID, name and state. Already-queued pull requests
return their blocking state check and any applicable queue check, without evaluating Git or other merge checks.
A failed queue configuration read fails the whole request with `500`, as for custom merge check results.

Returns `500` if custom merge checks are configured but their results aren't currently retrievable,
since the real merge action requires them too and would fail the same way.

<h3 id="list-pull-request-mergeability-checks-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|q|query|string|false|Only a limited subset of BBQL is supported here. Checks that are expensive to calculate can be excluded: `type!="git_mergeability_check"` skips Git conflict evaluation, and `check.kind!="maximum_commits_behind"` skips the bounded Git ancestry check behind that standard merge check. Combine both with `AND` (either order). Anything else returns `400 Bad Request`.|
|pull_request_id|path|integer|true|The id of the pull request.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "size": 0,
  "values": [
    {
      "type": "pullrequest_state_check",
      "status": "PASSED",
      "required": true,
      "blocking": true
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "error": {
    "message": "string",
    "detail": "string",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```
